title: Development Sprints With Agents, QA Reports, and Workspace
author: bunnyUFO
selftext:
Was inspired by this [Stefan 3D video about his workspace](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gV23ON8BgwU)

I used his repository [mr-mak-workspace](https://github.com/witnesstodark/mr-mak-workspace) as a starting point but did not fit my workflow much and self-hosted my own as a docker container.

I've made my own set of AI skills for the way I like to develop things and it involved the sessions/agents adding things to workspace during certain tasks like milestones reached, QA test reports, A/B testing (research).

I use my site to track progress, review possible bugs, brainstorm with mockups, and write hand-off documents so other sessions can pick up where one left off.

I have found that dumber models using a browser with restricted access to codebase, HTML/DOM, and JavaScript work great as QA. You can even ask them for qualitative data like "what did you like?" what "what was frustrating?". Then if a smarter model with context on repository reviews the QA report they can know what is a true bug, bad design decision, or a an AI delusion.
